words.enDefinition: a friendly greeting after a long time apart

examples.en: Hey Marco, long time no see! When did you get back from winter break?
examples.zh: 嗨，马可，「好久不见」！你寒假什么时候回来的？

examples.en: I ran into my old roommate at the library and we both said long time no see.
examples.zh: 我在图书馆偶遇了以前的室友，我们互相说了声「好久不见」。

words.enDefinition: a casual greeting that invites the other person's news

examples.en: Maya waved from across the quad and asked what's up before lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭前，玛雅从草坪对面朝我挥手，问我「最近怎么样」。

examples.en: What's up? I haven't seen you since the dorm barbecue.
examples.zh: 「最近怎么样」？宿舍烧烤之后我就一直没见过你。

words.enDefinition: a friendly question about how someone is doing

examples.en: I ran into my TA at the coffee cart and asked how's it going.
examples.zh: 我在咖啡摊碰到助教，顺口问了句「最近还好吗」。

examples.en: How's it going, Sam? I haven't seen you since move-in day.
examples.zh: 「最近还好吗」，山姆？开学搬入那天之后我就没见过你。

collocations: ask a classmate how's it going

words.enDefinition: asks about someone's life since you last met

examples.en: How have you been since you moved into the new apartment?
examples.zh: 搬进新公寓之后，你「过得怎么样」？

examples.en: My aunt called after my first month at university and asked, “How have you been?”
examples.zh: 我上大学满一个月时，阿姨打电话问：「最近过得怎么样？」

collocations: catch up with an old friend

words.enDefinition: says a long time has passed since you last met

examples.en: Hey Kevin, it's been a while since our last study session together.
examples.zh: 嗨，凯文，距离上次一起自习已经「好一阵子没见了」。

examples.en: It's been a while, so let's grab dinner and catch up properly.
examples.zh: 「好一阵子没见了」，我们找时间吃顿饭好好聊聊吧。

collocations: it's been a while since we talked

words.expression: What have you been up to?
words.lemma: what have you been up to?
words.enDefinition: asks what someone has been busy with recently
acceptedEnVariants: What have you been up to?
what have you been up to

examples.en: You disappeared from the group chat — what have you been up to?
examples.zh: 你从群聊里消失了好一阵子，「最近都在忙什么」？

examples.en: My cousin wrote, “What have you been up to?” after seeing my first campus photos.
examples.zh: 表哥看了我的第一批校园照片后发消息问：「最近都在忙些什么？」

collocations: ask what someone has been up to
share what you've been up to

words.enDefinition: a remark when you share an unexpected connection

examples.en: Wait, you took violin lessons from my aunt too? Small world!
examples.zh: 等等，你也跟我姨妈学过小提琴？这「世界真小」！

examples.en: When we discovered our moms were college roommates, we kept saying small world.
examples.zh: 发现我们的妈妈曾是大学室友时，我们不停感叹「世界真小」。

collocations: exclaim that it's a small world

words.enDefinition: said when the person just mentioned suddenly appears

examples.en: We were just complaining about the landlord, and speak of the devil, he texted.
examples.zh: 我们正吐槽房东呢，「说曹操曹操到」，他的消息就来了。

examples.en: Speak of the devil — here comes Jenny, and we were just talking about her.
examples.zh: 「说曹操曹操到」——我们正聊到珍妮，她就走过来了。

words.enDefinition: a polite greeting for meeting someone the first time

examples.en: At orientation, I shook hands with my lab partner and said nice to meet you.
examples.zh: 迎新会上，我和实验课搭档握手，说了声「很高兴认识你」。

examples.en: Nice to meet you — I'm the new exchange student from Shanghai.
examples.zh: 「很高兴认识你」，我是从上海来的新交换生。

collocations: reply nice to meet you too

words.enDefinition: a casual goodbye meaning see you soon

examples.en: Class starts in five minutes, so catch you later at the dining hall.
examples.zh: 五分钟后上课，食堂「待会儿见」。

examples.en: My teammate grabbed his skateboard and shouted catch you later before riding off.
examples.zh: 队友抓起滑板，喊了声「待会儿见」就滑走了。

words.enDefinition: a warm goodbye asking someone to look after themselves

examples.en: It's getting cold, so take care and text me when you're home.
examples.zh: 天气转凉了，「保重」，到家给我发个消息。

examples.en: She hugged me at the station and told me to take care on the trip.
examples.zh: 她在车站抱了抱我，叮嘱我旅途中「保重」。

words.enDefinition: a friendly goodbye wishing someone a nice day

examples.en: The barista handed me my latte and said have a good one with a smile.
examples.zh: 咖啡师递上我的拿铁，笑着说了句「祝你今天顺利」。

examples.en: Thanks for helping me move — have a good one, and see you Monday.
examples.zh: 谢谢你帮我搬家——「祝你今天顺利」，周一见。

words.enDefinition: a Friday goodbye wishing a pleasant weekend

examples.en: Before we packed up, my professor told the class to have a nice weekend.
examples.zh: 收拾书包前，教授祝全班同学「周末愉快」。

examples.en: Have a nice weekend, and don't forget we're hiking Saturday morning.
examples.zh: 「周末愉快」，别忘了周六早上我们还要去徒步。

collocations: say it before leaving on Friday

words.enDefinition: a send-off telling someone to enjoy an activity

examples.en: You're going to the concert tonight? Have fun, and take lots of pictures.
examples.zh: 你今晚去演唱会？「玩得开心」，多拍点照片。

examples.en: My parents told me to have fun at the welcome party for new students.
examples.zh: 爸妈叮嘱我在新生欢迎会上「玩得开心」。

words.expression: It was nice talking to you.
words.lemma: it was nice talking to you.
words.enDefinition: a polite closing line after an enjoyable chat
acceptedEnVariants: It was nice talking to you.
it was nice talking to you
it was great talking to you

examples.en: As I left the club fair, I told the senior it was nice talking to her.
examples.zh: 离开社团招新摊位时，我跟学姐说「跟你聊得很开心」。

examples.en: It was nice talking to you at the bus stop — here's my number.
examples.zh: 在公交站「跟你聊得很开心」——这是我的联系方式。

collocations: say it was nice talking to you

words.enDefinition: the standard polite reply when someone thanks you

examples.en: When I thanked her for the notes, she just smiled and said you're welcome.
examples.zh: 我谢她借我笔记时，她只是笑着说「不客气」。

examples.en: You're welcome — next time just ask me before the exam week starts.
examples.zh: 「不客气」——下次考试周开始前直接找我就行。

words.enDefinition: a relaxed reply showing helping was no trouble

examples.en: When I apologized for being five minutes late, my tutor said no problem.
examples.zh: 我为迟到五分钟道歉时，辅导老师说「没问题」。

examples.en: No problem, I can print the extra copies for our study group tonight.
examples.zh: 「没问题」，今晚我可以为学习小组多打印几份资料。

words.enDefinition: a friendly reply that you would help again whenever needed

examples.en: Thanks for printing my essay! Anytime — that's what dorm mates are for.
examples.zh: 谢谢你帮我打印论文！「随时乐意帮忙」，宿舍同学就该这样。

examples.en: When she thanked me for the ride to campus, I just said anytime.
examples.zh: 她谢我顺路带她去学校时，我说了句「随时都行」。

words.enDefinition: a polite reply showing you were happy to help

examples.en: After I helped him carry boxes upstairs, he thanked me and I said my pleasure.
examples.zh: 我帮他搬箱子上楼后，他道了谢，我说「乐意效劳」。

examples.en: My pleasure — you'd do the same for me if I locked myself out.
examples.zh: 「乐意效劳」——要是我被锁在门外，你也会这么帮我的。

words.enDefinition: a warm emphatic way to thank someone

examples.en: Thank you so much for lending me your laptop during finals week.
examples.zh: 期末周把电脑借给我，「非常感谢」。

examples.en: She said thank you so much when I helped her register for classes.
examples.zh: 我帮她完成选课注册后，她说了声「太感谢了」。

collocations: add it to a thank-you note

words.enDefinition: a friendly casual way to thank someone

examples.en: Thanks a lot for covering my dish duty while I was sick.
examples.zh: 我生病时你帮我值日洗碗，「多谢啦」。

examples.en: He passed me the worksheet and whispered thanks a lot before the quiz.
examples.zh: 测验前他递给我练习纸，小声说了句「多谢」。

words.enDefinition: expresses sincere gratitude for someone's help

examples.en: You drove me to the airport at six — I really appreciate it.
examples.zh: 你六点开车送我去机场——「真的太感谢了」。

examples.en: “I really appreciate it,” he said after I sent him the lecture notes.
examples.zh: 我把课堂笔记发给他后，他说：「我真的很感激。」

words.enDefinition: promises to return a favor in the future
acceptedEnVariants: I owe you one for this

examples.en: You covered my shift at the cafe? I owe you one, seriously.
examples.zh: 你替我上了咖啡馆的班？「我欠你个人情」，真的。

examples.en: “I owe you one,” I said when my roommate brought up my parcel.
examples.zh: 室友帮我把快递拿上楼时，我说：「欠你一个人情。」

words.enDefinition: a casual admission that you made a small mistake

examples.en: I grabbed your drink by mistake — my bad, they look exactly the same.
examples.zh: 我拿错了你的饮料——「我的错」，它们看起来一模一样。

examples.en: When my elbow knocked his pen off the desk, I whispered my bad.
examples.zh: 我的手肘把他的笔碰下桌时，我小声说了句「我的错」。

words.enDefinition: a light apology for a minor slip

examples.en: Sorry about that, I didn't realize my phone kept buzzing during the movie.
examples.zh: 「不好意思啊」，我没意识到看电影时我的手机一直在响。

examples.en: He stepped on my foot in the crowded bus and said sorry about that.
examples.zh: 拥挤的公交上他踩了我的脚，说了句「不好意思啊」。

words.enDefinition: comforts someone by saying mistakes are normal

examples.en: When I spilled coffee on my notes, my roommate shrugged and said it happens.
examples.zh: 我把咖啡洒在笔记上时，室友耸耸肩说「难免的，常有的事」。

examples.en: Don't beat yourself up over one failed quiz — it happens to everyone.
examples.zh: 别为一次测验失利太自责——「这种事谁都难免」。

words.enDefinition: tells someone to forget what you just said

examples.en: Never mind, I found my ID card at the bottom of my backpack.
examples.zh: 「没关系，不用麻烦了」，我在背包底部找到校园卡了。

examples.en: I started to ask about the fee, but the clerk said never mind and waived it.
examples.zh: 我刚想问手续费的事，柜员说「算了，不用了」，直接给我免了。

words.enDefinition: downplays a problem so the other person relaxes

examples.en: Lending you twenty dollars until Friday is no big deal, don't stress.
examples.zh: 借你二十美元到周五「没什么大不了的」，别有压力。

examples.en: I missed the free breakfast, but honestly it was no big deal at all.
examples.zh: 我没赶上免费早餐，但说真的，这「没什么大不了」。

words.enDefinition: shows you like and accept an idea

examples.en: Pizza night at eight? Sounds good, I'll bring some drinks over.
examples.zh: 晚上八点披萨之夜？「听起来不错」，我带点饮料过去。

examples.en: My roommate said the gym opens at six, and I said sounds good.
examples.zh: 室友说健身房六点开门，我回了句「听起来不错」。

words.enDefinition: confirms an agreement or bargain between two people

examples.en: You cook tonight and I do the dishes — deal, shake on it?
examples.zh: 今晚你做饭我洗碗——「一言为定」，击个掌？

examples.en: He offered to trade his Friday shift for my Sunday one, and I said deal.
examples.zh: 他提出用他的周五班换我的周日班，我答应道「成交」。

collocations: say deal to seal an agreement
strike a deal with a friend

words.enDefinition: readily agrees to do what someone asked

examples.en: When she asked me to water her plants, I said you got it.
examples.zh: 她请我帮忙浇花时，我爽快地说「包在我身上」。

examples.en: You got it — I'll save you a seat in the lecture hall at nine.
examples.zh: 「没问题，包在我身上」——九点我会在阶梯教室帮你占座。

words.enDefinition: a friendly way to agree to a request

examples.en: Sure thing, I'll forward you the professor's slides right after class.
examples.zh: 「好的，没问题」，下课后我马上把教授的幻灯片转发给你。

examples.en: When I asked him to grab me a coffee, he said sure thing.
examples.zh: 我请他帮我带杯咖啡时，他答应了声「好的，没问题」。

words.enDefinition: emphatically agrees or confirms without hesitation

examples.en: Are you coming to the game on Friday? You bet, front row seats.
examples.zh: 周五的比赛你来吗？「那当然」，我都买好前排票了。

examples.en: I asked whether she was joining the volunteering trip, and she said you bet.
examples.zh: 我问她去不去志愿活动，她干脆地说「那当然」。

words.enDefinition: readily agrees to a suggestion with casual enthusiasm

examples.en: There's a free yoga class tonight after practice — sure, why not?
examples.zh: 今晚练完有一节免费瑜伽课——「好啊，为什么不呢」？

examples.en: When I suggested trying the new ramen place, my friends said why not.
examples.zh: 我提议去尝尝新开的拉面店，朋友们说「好啊，走啊」。

words.enDefinition: asks to be included in a plan

examples.en: You're organizing a beach cleanup? Count me in for Saturday morning.
examples.zh: 你们要组织海滩清洁活动？周六早上「算我一个」。

examples.en: He heard about the board game night and immediately said count me in.
examples.zh: 听说有桌游之夜，他立刻说「算我一个」。

words.enDefinition: accepts the other person's point as reasonable

examples.en: You want to study first and hang out later? Fair enough.
examples.zh: 你想先学习再出去玩？「行吧，有道理」。

examples.en: I complained about the curfew, but after her explanation I said fair enough.
examples.zh: 我抱怨门禁太严，听完她的解释后我说「好吧，有道理」。

words.enDefinition: expresses complete agreement with someone's opinion

examples.en: I couldn't agree more — the campus gym definitely needs longer opening hours.
examples.zh: 「我完全赞同」——校园健身房确实需要延长开放时间。

examples.en: When she praised the new study lounge, I said I couldn't agree more.
examples.zh: 她夸新的自习室时，我说「再同意不过了」。

words.enDefinition: agrees strongly because you share the same experience

examples.en: When he complained about noon lines, I sighed and said tell me about it.
examples.zh: 他抱怨中午排长队时，我叹了口气说「可不是嘛」。

examples.en: Tell me about it — I waited twenty minutes just for a sandwich.
examples.zh: 「可不是嘛」——我光是买个三明治就排了二十分钟。

collocations: reply with tell me about it

words.enDefinition: politely declines an offer while staying friendly

examples.en: Would you like some more fries before the movie? I'm good, thanks.
examples.zh: 看电影前还要再来点薯条吗？「不用了，谢谢」。

examples.en: The vendor offered me a sample, but I smiled and said, “I'm good, thanks.”
examples.zh: 摊主请我试吃，我笑着说：「不用了，谢谢。」

collocations: say I'm good with a smile

words.enDefinition: softly declines while leaving the door open

examples.en: I have a lab report due tonight, so maybe next time for the movie.
examples.zh: 今晚要交实验报告，看电影就「下次吧」。

examples.en: She couldn't join the hotpot dinner, but she promised maybe next time.
examples.zh: 她来不了火锅聚餐，但答应说「下次一定」。

words.enDefinition: casually declines an offer or activity this time

examples.en: Karaoke until midnight? I'll pass, I have an eight a.m. lecture.
examples.zh: 唱卡拉OK到半夜？「这次就不去了」，我早上八点有课。

examples.en: Everyone signed up for the spicy food challenge, but I told them I'll pass.
examples.zh: 大家都报名吃辣挑战，我跟他们说我「就不参加了」。

words.enDefinition: a polite way to brush off someone's thanks

examples.en: Don't mention it — anyone would have lent you the lecture notes.
examples.zh: 「不用谢」——换谁都会把课堂笔记借给你的。

examples.en: When I thanked him for the ride, he waved and said don't mention it.
examples.zh: 我谢他顺路载我时，他摆摆手说「不用客气」。

words.enDefinition: buys time before deciding, often to decline gently

examples.en: When the club recruiter pressed me, I just said I'll think about it.
examples.zh: 社团招募的人一直催我，我只说「我考虑一下」。

examples.en: “I'll think about it,” I told my friend when she invited me on the weekend trip.
examples.zh: 朋友邀请我周末去旅行时，我说：“我会「考虑一下」。”

words.enDefinition: gives an undecided answer to avoid committing now

examples.en: Can we get a puppy next semester? We'll see how your grades look.
examples.zh: 下学期能养小狗吗？「到时候再说」，看你的成绩怎么样。

examples.en: I asked Dad about the road trip, and he just said we'll see.
examples.zh: 我问爸爸自驾游的事，他只说了句「到时候再说吧」。

words.enDefinition: checks someone's availability before making an invitation

examples.en: Are you free tonight? A few of us are playing basketball at seven.
examples.zh: 你「今晚有空吗」？我们几个七点要打篮球。

examples.en: She texted to ask if I was free tonight for a study session.
examples.zh: 她发消息问我「今晚有没有空」一起自习。

collocations: ask if someone is free tonight

words.enDefinition: invites someone to eat together casually
acceptedEnVariants: let's grab a bite to eat

examples.en: Let's grab a bite after chem lab — I know a cheap noodle place.
examples.zh: 化学实验课后我们「随便吃点吧」——我知道一家便宜的面馆。

examples.en: “Let's grab a bite,” she said as we left our afternoon class together.
examples.zh: 我们一起离开下午的课堂时，她说：“咱们去「随便吃点东西」吧。”

words.enDefinition: warmly accepts an invitation or opportunity

examples.en: Join us for board games on Friday? I'd love to.
examples.zh: 周五一起来玩桌游吗？「我很乐意去」。

examples.en: When my neighbor invited me hiking, I told her I'd love to come.
examples.zh: 邻居邀我去徒步时，我跟她说「很乐意一起」。

words.enDefinition: confirms that you will definitely attend

examples.en: Your graduation recital is at six? I'll be there, front and center.
examples.zh: 你的毕业演奏会在六点？「我一定到」，坐最前排。

examples.en: “I'll be there,” my flatmate said when I asked about the poster presentation.
examples.zh: 我问起海报展示时，室友说：“我「会到场」的。”

words.enDefinition: asks the other person to choose a convenient time
acceptedEnVariants: what time works best for you

examples.en: What time works for you — before breakfast or right after your morning class?
examples.zh: 你「什么时间方便」——早饭前还是早课后？

examples.en: To plan our group meeting, the leader asked what time worked for everyone.
examples.zh: 为了定小组会议时间，组长问大家「什么时间方便」。

collocations: find a time that suits everyone

words.enDefinition: promises to inform someone once you decide
acceptedEnVariants: I'll let you know by tonight

examples.en: Not sure about Saturday yet, but I'll let you know by tomorrow night.
examples.zh: 周六的事我还没定，但最晚明晚「我会告诉你」。

examples.en: “I'll let you know,” she replied as she opened her calendar to check Friday.
examples.zh: 她打开日历查看周五安排时回答：“我「再告诉你」。”

words.enDefinition: tells the other person they can make the choice

examples.en: Should we watch a comedy or a documentary? It's up to you.
examples.zh: 我们看喜剧还是纪录片？「由你决定」。

examples.en: “It’s up to you,” I told my roommate when she asked about dinner.
examples.zh: 室友问我晚饭怎么安排，我说：「由你决定。」

words.enDefinition: shows you have no preference between options

examples.en: Window seat or aisle? I don't mind, whatever is easier for you.
examples.zh: 靠窗还是靠过道？「我都行」，哪个方便选哪个。

examples.en: When asked whether to stay or head home, I said, “I don’t mind.”
examples.zh: 别人问是留下还是回家，我说：「我都行。」

collocations: say you don't mind either way

words.enDefinition: says any option is fine as long as it fits

examples.en: Meet at eight or eight thirty? Whatever works for your bus schedule.
examples.zh: 八点还是八点半碰头？按你的公交时间「怎么方便怎么来」。

examples.en: He said we could video call or just text, and I said whatever works.
examples.zh: 他说可以视频也可以发消息，我说「怎么方便怎么来」。

collocations: let the other person arrange it

words.enDefinition: tells someone to do whatever they prefer

examples.en: You won't wear a jacket in this wind? Suit yourself.
examples.zh: 这么大的风你不穿外套？「随你的便」。

examples.en: When I refused a second helping, my host laughed and said suit yourself.
examples.zh: 我谢绝再来一份时，房东笑着说了句「随你便」。

words.enDefinition: asks someone to repeat because you did not hear

examples.en: Pardon me? The announcement was too soft to hear over the rain.
examples.zh: 「你说什么」？广播声音太小，雨声太大听不清。

examples.en: Pardon me? Did you just say the seminar starts at eight?
examples.zh: 「你说什么」？你是说研讨课八点开始？

words.enDefinition: asks for repetition after missing what was said

examples.en: Sorry, I didn't catch your room number — this hallway echo is terrible.
examples.zh: 「不好意思，我没听清」你的房间号——走廊回音太大了。

examples.en: Sorry, I didn't catch that — the line kept breaking up on the bus.
examples.zh: 「不好意思，我没听清」——公交上信号一直断断续续。

words.expression: Could you say that more slowly?
words.lemma: could you say that more slowly?
words.enDefinition: requests a slower repeat to follow better
acceptedEnVariants: Could you say that more slowly?
could you say that more slowly

examples.en: Could you say that more slowly? I want to write down the room number.
examples.zh: 您能「说得慢一点吗」？我想记下教室门牌号。

examples.en: Could you say that more slowly — my notebook is still on question two.
examples.zh: 您能「说得慢一点吗」——我的笔记还停在第二题。

words.enDefinition: asks someone to explain their point more clearly
acceptedEnVariants: what do you mean by that

examples.en: What do you mean the pool is closed? We just checked the app.
examples.zh: 「你是什么意思」，游泳池关了？我们刚看过应用。

examples.en: “What do you mean?” I asked when my tutor mentioned the essay structure.
examples.zh: 辅导老师提到文章结构时，我问：「你指的是什么？」

collocations: what do you mean by that

words.enDefinition: politely says you have not understood an explanation

examples.en: I don't quite follow — could you explain the second step of the proof again?
examples.zh: 「我没太听懂」——证明的第二步能再讲一遍吗？

examples.en: “I don't quite follow,” I said when the tutor moved to the next equation.
examples.zh: 老师开始讲下一个方程时，我说：“我「没太跟上」。”

collocations: lose the thread of a talk

words.enDefinition: softens a statement you are not fully sure about

examples.en: Correct me if I'm wrong, but the seminar was moved to Thursday, right?
examples.zh: 「如果我说错了请指正」——研讨会改到周四了，对吧？

examples.en: Correct me if I'm wrong, but you mentioned a group discount for students.
examples.zh: 「如果我说错了请指正」——你之前提到过学生团体折扣。

words.enDefinition: confirms you have understood a message or instruction

examples.en: When the shift manager texted the rota, I replied got it right away.
examples.zh: 排班经理把班表发来后，我马上回复「收到」。

examples.en: Got it, so we submit the group project by Friday noon, right?
examples.zh: 「明白了」，小组项目周五中午前提交，对吧？

collocations: reply got it to a message

words.enDefinition: shows you now understand what was explained

examples.en: Oh, I see — the discount only applies to the student meal plan.
examples.zh: 「哦，原来如此」——这个折扣只适用于学生套餐。

examples.en: He explained the shuttle route twice before I finally said I see.
examples.zh: 他把班车路线讲了两遍，我才终于说「明白了」。

words.enDefinition: a polite reply to useful information

examples.en: The cafeteria closes early on Fridays? Good to know, thanks for telling me.
examples.zh: 食堂周五提前关门？「学到了」，谢谢你告诉我。

examples.en: When my senior warned me about surprise quizzes, I said good to know.
examples.zh: 学姐提醒我那门课常有突击测验，我说「多谢告知」。

words.enDefinition: shows a fact suddenly explains something confusing

examples.en: No wonder you're exhausted — you only slept four hours before the exam.
examples.zh: 「怪不得」你累成这样——考试前只睡了四个小时。

examples.en: The bus didn't stop today, and no wonder, since it's a public holiday.
examples.zh: 今天公交不停靠，「难怪」——今天是公共假期。

words.enDefinition: restates an idea in simpler or clearer words

examples.en: In other words, we can skip chapter five since it won't be tested.
examples.zh: 「换句话说」，第五章可以跳过，因为不考。

examples.en: The TA put the grading rule in other words so the freshmen could follow.
examples.zh: 助教「换了个说法」讲评分规则，好让新生听懂。

words.enDefinition: skips the details and gives only the main point
acceptedEnVariants: to make a long story short

examples.en: Long story short, we missed the last bus and walked home in the rain.
examples.zh: 「长话短说」，我们没赶上末班车，冒雨走回了家。

examples.en: She told the whole tale, but long story short, they missed the flight.
examples.zh: 她从头讲了一遍，但「简单说」，他们误机了。

collocations: to make a long story short

words.enDefinition: says while handing something to someone

examples.en: Here you go — one iced americano and a blueberry muffin.
examples.zh: 「给，您拿好」——一杯冰美式和一个蓝莓麦芬。

examples.en: The librarian scanned my card, handed over the book, and said here you go.
examples.zh: 图书管理员扫了我的卡，把书递过来，说了句「给你」。

collocations: pass an item across the counter

words.enDefinition: says while handing something over, often with a smile

examples.en: There you go, one chicken wrap — that'll be eight fifty total.
examples.zh: 「给，拿好了」——一份鸡肉卷，一共八块五。

examples.en: He tightened the last screw on my chair, handed it back, and said there you go.
examples.zh: 他拧紧椅子的最后一颗螺丝递还给我，说了句「好了，拿去」。

words.enDefinition: politely lets someone go through a door first

examples.en: He held the dorm door with his elbow and said after you.
examples.zh: 他用胳膊肘撑住宿舍门，说了声「你先请」。

examples.en: After you, I insist — you were waiting in line much longer than me.
examples.zh: 「您先请」——您排队的时间比我长得多。

words.enDefinition: shows strong disbelief at surprising news

examples.en: No way! You got the internship at the design studio in New York?
examples.zh: 「不会吧」！你拿到纽约设计工作室的实习了？

examples.en: When I told him the concert tickets were free, he shouted no way twice.
examples.zh: 我说演唱会门票免费时，他连喊了两声「真的假的」。

words.enDefinition: reacts to news too surprising to be true

examples.en: You're kidding! The professor canceled the quiz and extended the deadline?
examples.zh: 「你不是开玩笑吧」！教授取消了测验还延后了截止日期？

examples.en: She announced she had won the essay prize, and I blurted out you're kidding!
examples.zh: 她宣布获得征文奖时，我脱口而出「你在开玩笑吧」！

words.enDefinition: a mild exclamation of surprise or shock
acceptedEnVariants: oh my gosh, look at that

examples.en: Oh my gosh, your presentation slides look so professional now.
examples.zh: 「我的天哪」，你的演讲幻灯片现在看起来太专业了。

examples.en: When the fire alarm went off at dawn, everyone groaned oh my gosh.
examples.zh: 清晨火警响起时，大家都哀嚎「我的天哪」。

words.enDefinition: reacts happily to positive news

examples.en: That's great news — your scholarship application went through on the first try.
examples.zh: 「太好了」——你的奖学金申请一次就通过了。

examples.en: She texted that the landlord accepted our offer, and I replied that's great news!
examples.zh: 她发消息说房东接受了我们的报价，我回复「这消息太好了」！

words.enDefinition: congratulates someone warmly on their good fortune

examples.en: I'm so happy for you — a paid research assistantship in your first year!
examples.zh: 「真为你高兴」——大一就拿到带薪研究助理岗位！

examples.en: “I'm so happy for you,” she said when I told her I had been accepted.
examples.zh: 我告诉她自己被录取时，她说：“我「真替你高兴」。”

words.enDefinition: responds warmly to positive news

examples.en: Your grandma is out of the hospital? Good to hear, send her my best.
examples.zh: 你奶奶出院了？「听到这个真好」，代我向她问好。

examples.en: When he said the tutoring had finally clicked, I smiled and said good to hear.
examples.zh: 他说辅导终于见效时，我笑着说「那就好」。

words.enDefinition: expresses sympathy after hearing bad news

examples.en: I'm sorry to hear that your internship offer fell through at the last minute.
examples.zh: 听说你的实习录用最后黄了，「我很难过」。

examples.en: When I mentioned my grandfather was ill, my roommate said she was sorry to hear that.
examples.zh: 提到爷爷生病时，室友说听到这个消息「她也很难过」。

words.enDefinition: encourages someone right before a challenge

examples.en: You've got this — you've rehearsed the presentation at least ten times already.
examples.zh: 「你能行的」——这个演讲你已经排练了至少十遍。

examples.en: My roommate squeezed my hand before the driving test and said you've got this.
examples.zh: 路考前室友握着我的手说「你一定行」。

words.enDefinition: wishes someone success before an exam or event

examples.en: Good luck with your driving test this afternoon — you've practiced plenty.
examples.zh: 下午路考「祝你好运」——你练习得够多了。

examples.en: The whole dorm floor wished me good luck before my scholarship interview.
examples.zh: 奖学金面试前，整层宿舍楼的同学都「祝我好运」。

words.enDefinition: a fun way to wish a performer good luck

examples.en: Break a leg at the spring concert — your solo is going to shine.
examples.zh: 春季音乐会上「祝你演出成功」——你的独奏一定会大放光彩。

examples.en: Backstage, the whole cast told the nervous lead singer to break a leg.
examples.zh: 后台里，全体演员都叮嘱紧张的领唱「演出顺利」。

words.enDefinition: hopes that something will go well

examples.en: Results come out tomorrow — fingers crossed that I passed organic chemistry.
examples.zh: 成绩明天公布——「祈祷好运」，希望有机化学过了。

examples.en: He sent the application at midnight and texted me saying fingers crossed.
examples.zh: 他半夜提交了申请，然后给我发消息说「求顺利」。

words.enDefinition: encourages someone struggling through a difficult time
acceptedEnVariants: hang in there, it gets better

examples.en: Finals week is brutal, but hang in there — only three exams left.
examples.zh: 考试周确实难熬，但「坚持住」——只剩三门了。

examples.en: When she wanted to quit the debate team, her coach told her to hang in there.
examples.zh: 她想退出辩论队时，教练让她「再撑一撑」。

collocations: hang in there a bit longer

words.enDefinition: praises someone for doing something exactly right

examples.en: You nailed it — your saxophone solo got the loudest applause of the night.
examples.zh: 「你吹得太棒了」——你的萨克斯独奏赢得了当晚最热烈的掌声。

examples.en: After my roommate's job interview, we all agreed she totally nailed it.
examples.zh: 室友面试回来后，我们都说她「表现得非常出色」。

words.enDefinition: praises someone for finishing a task very well

examples.en: Well done on the debate — your closing argument was really powerful.
examples.zh: 辩论赛「干得好」——你的结辩陈词非常有力量。

examples.en: Our coach clapped and said well done after the relay team won gold.
examples.zh: 接力队夺金后，教练拍着手连声说「干得漂亮」。

collocations: say well done with a smile

words.enDefinition: praises someone's achievement or brave choice

examples.en: You finally signed up for the debate team? Good for you!
examples.zh: 你终于报名辩论队了？「真有你的」！

examples.en: When I told her I quit energy drinks, she said good for you.
examples.zh: 我说自己戒了功能饮料，她说「干得好」。

words.enDefinition: comforts someone after a loss or failure

examples.en: You lost the student election by twelve votes — better luck next time.
examples.zh: 学生会选举你只差十二票——「下次会更好的」。

examples.en: He missed the bus by a minute, and I joked better luck next time.
examples.zh: 他差一分钟没赶上公交，我开玩笑说「下次手速快点」。

words.enDefinition: wishes a sick person a quick recovery

examples.en: Get well soon — the dorm feels way too quiet without you around.
examples.zh: 「早日康复」——没有你在，宿舍实在太安静了。

examples.en: We signed the card for our sick roommate and wrote get well soon inside.
examples.zh: 我们给生病的室友在贺卡里写下「祝早日康复」。

words.enDefinition: thankfully reacts to an unexpected gift or favor

examples.en: Birthday cupcakes on my study desk? You shouldn't have, but thank you.
examples.zh: 书桌上放着生日纸杯蛋糕？「你太客气了」，谢谢你。

examples.en: When my host family handed me a parting gift, I kept saying you shouldn't have.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭送我临别礼物时，我连声说「你们太客气了」。

words.enDefinition: thanks a host when leaving their home or event

examples.en: Thanks for having me over — the dumplings we made together were delicious.
examples.zh: 「多谢款待」——我们一起包的饺子太好吃了。

examples.en: At the door, every guest thanked the host family for having them.
examples.zh: 临走时每位客人都感谢寄宿家庭的「盛情招待」。

words.enDefinition: tells a guest to relax and feel comfortable

examples.en: Make yourself at home — the remote is on the coffee table.
examples.zh: 「别拘束，随意」——遥控器在茶几上。

examples.en: “Make yourself at home,” my aunt told the exchange student when he arrived.
examples.zh: 交换生到家时，姨妈说：「随意一点，别拘束。」

words.enDefinition: invites a guest to serve food or drinks freely

examples.en: Help yourself to the fruit bowl — the mangoes are extra sweet today.
examples.zh: 果盘「随便吃」——今天的芒果特别甜。

examples.en: She pointed at the fruit on the table and said, “Help yourself.”
examples.zh: 她指着桌上的水果说：「想吃就自己拿。」

words.enDefinition: politely gets attention or pardons a small interruption

examples.en: Excuse me, is this seat taken? The row looks almost empty.
examples.zh: 「打扰一下」，这个座位有人吗？这一排看起来几乎空着。

examples.en: She said excuse me twice while squeezing past the crowded bookshelves.
examples.zh: 挤过拥挤的书架时，她说了两声「借过」。

words.enDefinition: gives permission for someone to start or continue

examples.en: Go ahead, ask the professor about the extra credit — he doesn't bite.
examples.zh: 「去吧」，去问教授加分的事——他人很和善。

examples.en: When I reached for the last cookie, my roommate said go ahead.
examples.zh: 我伸手拿最后一块饼干时，室友说「你拿吧」。

words.enDefinition: warmly gives permission to use or do something
acceptedEnVariants: feel free to borrow my notes

examples.en: Feel free to use my printer whenever the library one is busy.
examples.zh: 图书馆打印机排队时，「尽管用」我的打印机。

examples.en: He said I should feel free to message him about internship questions.
examples.zh: 他说实习方面的问题「随时可以」找他。

collocations: invite someone to use your things

words.enDefinition: softens a comment that might sound rude

examples.en: No offense, but your essay would read better with shorter sentences.
examples.zh: 「无意冒犯」，你的文章多用短句读起来会更顺。

examples.en: He started with no offense, then said the movie was way too long.
examples.zh: 他先说了句「别介意我直说」，然后说这部电影实在太长了。

words.enDefinition: warmly gives someone permission to go first or use something

examples.en: Be my guest — take the window seat, I prefer the aisle anyway.
examples.zh: 「你请便」——坐靠窗吧，反正我更喜欢过道。

examples.en: When I reached for the last slice, my roommate said be my guest.
examples.zh: 我伸手拿最后一块披萨时，室友说「你先用」。

words.enDefinition: casually offers to help someone with a task
acceptedEnVariants: need a hand with those boxes

examples.en: Need a hand carrying those suitcases up to the fourth floor?
examples.zh: 需要「帮忙」把这几个箱子搬上四楼吗？

examples.en: He saw me struggling with the projector and asked if I needed a hand.
examples.zh: 他见我摆弄投影仪很费劲，问我要不要「搭把手」。

words.enDefinition: casually says you would appreciate some help
acceptedEnVariants: I could use a hand with this

examples.en: I could use a hand moving this sofa — it's heavier than it looks.
examples.zh: 搬这个沙发我需要「有人搭把手」——它比看起来沉多了。

examples.en: “I could use a hand,” she called as she tried to set up the booth.
examples.zh: 她试着布置摊位时喊了一声：“我「需要搭把手」。”

collocations: could use a hand with the move
request an extra pair of hands

words.expression: Let me know if you need anything.
words.lemma: let me know if you need anything.
words.enDefinition: kindly offers help for whenever it might be needed
acceptedEnVariants: Let me know if you need anything.
let me know if you need anything
let me know if you need anything else

examples.en: Get some rest after the clinic — let me know if you need anything.
examples.zh: 看完病回来好好休息——「有事随时跟我说」。

examples.en: My neighbor promised to let me know if she needed anything while I was away.
examples.zh: 邻居答应我出差期间她「有需要会叫我」。

words.enDefinition: confidently takes over a task for someone

examples.en: You focus on your interview — leave it to me to book the taxi.
examples.zh: 你专心准备面试——订车的事「交给我吧」。

examples.en: When the printer jammed before class, he said leave it to me and fixed it.
examples.zh: 课前打印机卡纸时，他说「交给我」并修好了。

collocations: leave it to me, don't worry

words.enDefinition: insists on paying for a shared meal or treat

examples.en: Put your wallet away — it's on me to celebrate your birthday.
examples.zh: 把钱包收起来——庆祝你生日，「这顿我请」。

examples.en: “It’s on me,” he said, picking up the bill before I could reach it.
examples.zh: 他先拿到了账单，说：「这顿算我的。」

words.enDefinition: suggests each person pays for their own share

examples.en: Let's go Dutch on dinner so nobody has to cover a huge bill.
examples.zh: 晚饭我们「AA制吧」，谁都不用替别人付大账单。

examples.en: “Let’s go Dutch,” my friend suggested when the waiter brought the bill over.
examples.zh: 服务员拿来账单时，朋友提议：「咱们各付各的。」

words.enDefinition: wishes diners a pleasant meal before they eat

examples.en: Your table is ready — enjoy your meal, and call me for refills.
examples.zh: 你们的桌子好了——「用餐愉快」，需要续杯叫我。

examples.en: The server smiled, put down two bowls of ramen, and said enjoy your meal.
examples.zh: 服务员笑着端上两碗拉面，说了句「请慢用」。

words.enDefinition: says in an exaggerated way that you are very hungry

examples.en: I skipped breakfast and back-to-back lectures — I'm starving right now.
examples.zh: 我没吃早饭又连着上课——现在「饿死了」。

examples.en: “I'm starving,” my roommate said while we stood in line at the food truck.
examples.zh: 我们在餐车旁排队时，室友说：“我「快饿死了」。”

words.enDefinition: a toast said before drinking together

examples.en: Cheers to surviving finals week — here's to our hard-earned break.
examples.zh: 「干杯」，庆祝熬过考试周——敬我们应得的假期。

examples.en: He clinked glasses with everyone and said cheers to our new roommate.
examples.zh: 他和每个人碰杯，说「为我们新室友干杯」。

words.enDefinition: casually says you are completely exhausted

examples.en: Two football practices and a lab report — I'm beat tonight.
examples.zh: 两场足球训练加一份实验报告——今晚我「累坏了」。

examples.en: “I'm beat,” he said, dropping onto the sofa after carrying boxes up three flights.
examples.zh: 搬着箱子爬了三段楼梯后，他一屁股坐到沙发上说：“我「累趴了」。”

words.enDefinition: texts that you have left and are traveling there

examples.en: I'm on my way — just wait for me at the cinema entrance.
examples.zh: 「我在路上了」——你在电影院门口等我一下。

examples.en: She texted that she was on her way but stuck in traffic.
examples.zh: 她发消息说「已经在路上」，只是堵车。

words.enDefinition: says you will arrive at the meeting spot very soon

examples.en: Order my milk tea please — I'm almost there, like two minutes.
examples.zh: 先帮我点奶茶——我「马上就到」，大约两分钟。

examples.en: He kept texting I'm almost there, but the bus was still ten stops away.
examples.zh: 他一直发消息说「快到了」，可公交还有十站路。

words.enDefinition: warns that you will arrive later than planned

examples.en: I'm running late — the seminar bus hasn't shown up yet.
examples.zh: 「我要迟到了」——研讨课的班车还没来。

examples.en: “I'm running late,” she texted from the bus, asking us to order without her.
examples.zh: 她在公交车上发消息：“我「要迟到了」，你们先点吧。”

words.enDefinition: politely announces that it is time to leave

examples.en: It's past ten and my bus leaves soon — I should get going.
examples.zh: 已经十点多，班车快发了——「我该走了」。

examples.en: “I should get going,” he said when he saw the time on his phone.
examples.zh: 他看到手机上的时间，说：“我「该走了」。”

words.enDefinition: suggests stopping the current work or activity for now

examples.en: We've finished four slides since noon — let's call it a day.
examples.zh: 从中午到现在我们做完了四页幻灯片——「今天就到这儿吧」。

examples.en: “Let's call it a day,” our tutor suggested after we finished the third practice test.
examples.zh: 做完第三套模拟题后，老师提议：“今天就「到这儿吧」。”

words.enDefinition: notes that arriving late still beats not coming

examples.en: You missed the opening ceremony but made the photo — better late than never.
examples.zh: 你错过了开幕式但赶上了合影——「迟到总比不到好」。

examples.en: He finally emailed the essay a week late, mumbling better late than never.
examples.zh: 他晚了一周才发来文章，嘟囔着「有总比没有好」。

words.enDefinition: reports that progress is fine up to now

examples.en: The roommates take turns cooking, and so far so good — no arguments yet.
examples.zh: 室友们轮流做饭，目前「一切顺利」——还没吵过架。

examples.en: It's day two of his study plan, and so far so good.
examples.zh: 这是他学习计划的第二天，目前为止「一切顺利」。

collocations: ask how it's going so far

words.enDefinition: introduces a new topic you just thought of

examples.en: By the way, did you finish signing up for the spring workshop?
examples.zh: 「顺便问一下」，春季工作坊你报上名了吗？

examples.en: By the way, your bike light is still clipped to my backpack.
examples.zh: 「对了」，你的车灯还别在我的背包上。

words.enDefinition: jumps to a related thing you suddenly remember

examples.en: That reminds me — we still need to return Professor Lee's projector.
examples.zh: 「这倒提醒我了」——我们还欠着李教授的投影仪没还。

examples.en: She mentioned buying envelopes, and that reminded me to mail my rent check.
examples.zh: 她提到买信封，「这倒提醒了我」该去寄房租支票了。

words.enDefinition: says something is starting or has finally arrived

examples.en: Here we go — our group presentation is the first one on stage.
examples.zh: 「开始了」——我们小组的展示第一个上场。

examples.en: The professor dimmed the lights, loaded the slides, and said here we go.
examples.zh: 教授调暗灯光、放好幻灯片，说了声「开始吧」。

words.enDefinition: asks someone to wait for a very short moment

examples.en: Hold on a second — I'm still looking for my student ID card.
examples.zh: 「稍等一下」——我还在找我的学生证。

examples.en: She asked me to hold on a second while she grabbed her keys.
examples.zh: 她让我「稍等片刻」，好去拿钥匙。

words.enDefinition: buys a moment while you think or check
acceptedEnVariants: let me see, where did I put it

examples.en: Let me see — the cheapest flight is either Tuesday or Thursday night.
examples.zh: 「让我看看」——最便宜的航班在周二或周四晚上。

examples.en: He paused, said let me see, and scrolled through his phone calendar.
examples.zh: 他停顿了一下，说了句「让我想想」，然后翻看手机日历。

words.enDefinition: says you are ready to listen with full attention

examples.en: You said you found a cheaper apartment? I'm all ears.
examples.zh: 你说找到了更便宜的公寓？「我洗耳恭听」。

examples.en: “I'm all ears,” I told my lab partner when she offered to explain the result.
examples.zh: 实验搭档主动提出给我解释结果时，我说：“我「洗耳恭听」。”

words.enDefinition: builds excitement before sharing surprising news

examples.en: Guess what? The campus cafe is giving out free smoothies today.
examples.zh: 「你猜怎么着」？校园咖啡店今天免费发放冰沙。

examples.en: She burst into the room shouting guess what before telling us her news.
examples.zh: 她冲进房间喊着「你猜怎么着」，然后才公布消息。

words.enDefinition: clarifies your real meaning before it sounds negative
acceptedEnVariants: don't get me wrong, I like it

examples.en: Don't get me wrong — I love the apartment, but the rent is too high.
examples.zh: 「别误会」——我很喜欢这套公寓，只是租金太高。

examples.en: He insisted, don't get me wrong, that he respected her final decision.
examples.zh: 他强调「别误会」，他尊重她的最终决定。

words.enDefinition: introduces advice by imagining yourself in their place

examples.en: If I were you, I'd email the professor before skipping tomorrow's lab.
examples.zh: 「要是我的话」，会先给教授发邮件说明，再翘明天的实验课。

examples.en: “If I were you, I would join the exchange program,” my sister said.
examples.zh: 姐姐说：「换作我是你」，我会参加交换项目。

collocations: if I were you, I'd start early

words.enDefinition: asks for someone's opinion about your idea
acceptedEnVariants: what do you think about it

examples.en: I want to paint the dorm door navy blue — what do you think?
examples.zh: 我想把宿舍门漆成深蓝色——「你觉得怎么样」？

examples.en: She held up her new poster and asked, “What do you think?”
examples.zh: 她举起新海报问：「你觉得怎么样？」

collocations: what do you think of my idea

words.enDefinition: asks for the story behind a sudden situation

examples.en: Why is the hallway flooded? What happened while I was in class?
examples.zh: 走廊怎么全是水？我上课的时候「发生什么了」？

examples.en: He rushed over, saw the broken window, and immediately asked what had happened.
examples.zh: 他冲过来看到碎玻璃，立刻问「出了什么事」。

words.enDefinition: checks on someone who looks upset, hurt, or unwell
acceptedEnVariants: are you okay, you look pale

examples.en: You look pale after the chemistry practical — are you okay, or should we see a doctor?
examples.zh: 化学实验后你脸色发白——「你还好吗」？要不要去看医生？

examples.en: I noticed my deskmate wiping tears, so I quietly asked are you okay.
examples.zh: 我注意到同桌在抹眼泪，便轻声问「你还好吗」。
